title: Authoring's remainder goes too: the consumer-patch fold, fragment provenance and the cold-oracle script
situation: Code review of 0330's change found authoring code still present that nothing shipped or used in cratylus's own development reaches: the consumer-patch fold (patches, their ops and errors, the resolved-body substitution, per-fragment provenance and the published resolve subpath), reachable only through the removed configuration file and explain. The same change removed canon's cold-oracle script and forge's validate driver, which 0330 did not name: the script ran cold reads through a Claude configuration directory, a harness cratylus no longer supports, and cratylus's own cold reads run through the repository's omp cold-reader script.
decision: The consumer-patch fold, fragment provenance and the resolve subpath are removed with their tests; discovery keeps its reference-graph check. The cold-oracle script and forge's validate driver stay removed. A plugin other than the corpus the command is built with is not something cratylus offers; the schema package's README addresses cratylus's contributors, never a corpus author. A check pins that install ignores a configuration file in its working directory.
consequences: Completes 0330. The cold-decode-oracle stance and the cold read concept are unaffected: they name a practice, not the removed script.
